entries.lesson_title: Fourier Transform of an LTI System Output
entries.core_move: Derive the Fourier-domain output relation $Y(j\omega)=X(j\omega)H(j\omega)$ by applying the Fourier transform to the LTI convolution equation and identifying $H(j\omega)$ as the transform of the impulse response.
Compute the time-domain output of an LTI system by forming $Y(j\omega)=X(j\omega)H(j\omega)$, simplifying the product, and applying the inverse Fourier transform.

entries.lesson_title: Comparing Direct Convolution and Frequency-Domain Multiplication
entries.core_move: Choose between direct convolution and frequency-domain multiplication by comparing the time-domain overlap integral with the transform-pair, multiplication, and inverse-transform workload.

entries.lesson_title: Periodic Inputs Through an LTI System
entries.core_move: Compute the output of an LTI system for a periodic input by scaling each Fourier-series harmonic coefficient by the frequency response at that harmonic, $Y_k=H(jk\omega_0)X_k$.

entries.lesson_title: Aperiodic Inputs Through an LTI System
entries.core_move: Compute the output of an LTI system for an aperiodic input by transforming the input to $X(j\omega)$, multiplying by $H(j\omega)$, and inverting $Y(j\omega)=X(j\omega)H(j\omega)$ to recover $y(t)$.
Select and apply either convolution or frequency-response multiplication to compute a continuous-time LTI system output from the input type and available system description.
